title: I built a flying-island fortress combat game in ~3 weeks with Claude Code + Blender MCP — here's the result
author: GurusCZ
selftext:
**Island Warfare**: humanity lives on floating islands after a catastrophe, and islands fight by shooting and ramming each other. Damage carves the voxel terrain away, building makes your island bigger. If you lose your lift crystal, the island sinks.

**How AI was used:**

* **Code:** Unity 6 / URP, written almost entirely through Claude Code. Voxel carving, AI opponents, campaign, builder, split screen.
* **3D models:** made in Blender through the Blender MCP, with Claude scripting the models. I checked every one before it went into the game.
* **Workflow:** one `PLAN.md` file as the single source of truth, with milestones M0–M32 and a play test after each one. Found bugs, report them, rinse and repeat. 
* **What I did myself:** design decisions, all play testing, feedback, music *(adjust this to what is true)*.

**What worked / what didn't:**

* ✅ Fast iteration: a feature in the morning, a play test in the afternoon.
* ✅ Procedural systems (voxel destruction, island generator) came out surprisingly solid.
* ❌ Batch builds once hung and needed a hard timeout.
* ❌ The look came from Asset Store packs but soon I switch to modelling in Blender. AI alone wouldn't have produced a consistent style.
